entries.name: KIDCB$
entries.purpose: keyboard device control block, 8 bytes; this entry names its first byte
entries.note: the block spans 4015H-401CH (ldos51 6-32); the ROM variables CAPSLOCK (4019H) and CURBLINK (401CH) lie inside it and keep their ROM names

entries.name: DODCB$
entries.purpose: video device control block, 8 bytes; this entry names its first byte
entries.note: the block spans 401DH-4024H (ldos51 6-32); the ROM variables CURADDR (4020H) and CURCHAR (4023H) lie inside it and keep their ROM names

entries.name: PRDCB$
entries.purpose: printer device control block, 8 bytes; this entry names its first byte
entries.note: the block spans 4025H-402CH (ldos51 6-32); the ROM variables PRTPAGELEN (4028H), PRTLINECNT (4029H), and PRTWIDTH (402BH) lie inside it and keep their ROM names

entries.name: @EXIT
entries.purpose: return to LDOS READY

entries.name: @ABORT
entries.purpose: abort the program and return to LDOS

entries.name: @DVRHK
entries.purpose: device-driver hook the ROM reaches for byte-level device I/O

entries.name: @ADTSK
entries.purpose: install a task to run at interrupt level

entries.name: @RMTSK
entries.purpose: uninstall an interrupt-level task

entries.name: @RPTSK
entries.purpose: give the task now running a different vector

entries.name: @KLTSK
entries.purpose: drop the task that is running

entries.name: DBGSV$
entries.purpose: DEBUG and system storage, not for programs

entries.name: @CKDRV
entries.purpose: check that a disk drive is available
entries.note: the Model III text edition of the manual lists @CKDRV at 4290H and has no @RAMDIR; this edition prints 4209H here and in the alphabetical listing (6-35), and 4290H for @RAMDIR (6-33)

entries.name: @ICNFG
entries.purpose: initialize the system configuration

entries.name: INBUF$
entries.purpose: 64-byte buffer for the user's command line

entries.name: JFCB$
entries.purpose: file control block the DO processor uses for JCL
entries.note: the map prints only the start address; the Model I map gives the block as 32 bytes (6-30)

entries.name: @KITSK
entries.purpose: task-processing entry used while the keyboard is scanned

entries.name: TIMER$
entries.purpose: heartbeat that ticks every 33.333 ms

entries.name: DFLAG$
entries.purpose: system device flag

entries.name: @LOGOT
entries.purpose: display a message and also write it to the job log

entries.name: @LOGER
entries.purpose: write a message to the job log

entries.name: @RAMDIR
entries.purpose: load directory records, or the free-space figure, into a RAM buffer
entries.note: the Model III text edition of the manual has @CKDRV at this address (see @CKDRV); TRSDOS 1.3 also puts its $RAMDIR here (trsdos13 84)

entries.name: @FNAME
entries.purpose: fetch a file's name and extension from its directory entry

entries.name: @CMD
entries.purpose: prompt for the next command
entries.note: the Model I map has @CMD at 4400H (6-35)

entries.name: @CMNDI
entries.purpose: jump into the command interpreter

entries.name: KFLAG$
entries.purpose: system keyboard flag
entries.note: the Model III map does not list it; the alphabetical listing (6-35) gives this address, as does the text on page 4-3 (X'429F'), and the purpose is the Model I map's for the same label (6-30)

entries.name: SFCB$
entries.purpose: file control block for loading system overlays
entries.note: the map prints only the start address; the Model I map gives the block as 20 bytes (6-31)

entries.name: @DOKEY
entries.purpose: vector for keyboard input from JCL while DO is running
entries.note: the Model III map does not list it; the alphabetical listing (6-35) gives this address, and the purpose is the Model I map's for the same label (6-31)

entries.name: KISV$
entries.purpose: saved vector of the KI (keyboard) device

entries.name: DOSV$
entries.purpose: saved vector of the DO (video) device

entries.name: PRSV$
entries.purpose: saved vector of the PR (printer) device

entries.name: KIJCL$
entries.purpose: saved vector of the KIJCL device

entries.name: JLDCB$
entries.purpose: device control block of the job log

entries.name: SIDCB$
entries.purpose: device control block of standard input

entries.name: SODCB$
entries.purpose: device control block of standard output

entries.name: S1DCB$
entries.purpose: spare device control block

entries.name: S2DCB$
entries.purpose: spare device control block

entries.name: S3DCB$
entries.purpose: spare device control block

entries.name: S4DCB$
entries.purpose: spare device control block

entries.name: SBUFF$
entries.purpose: buffer of 256 bytes the system uses for disk transfers

entries.name: EXTDBG$
entries.purpose: vector to the extended DEBUG

entries.name: @MSG
entries.purpose: route a message line to its output device

entries.name: @DBGHK
entries.purpose: hook used by DEBUG, off limits to programs

entries.name: @ERROR
entries.purpose: display the message for a DOS error code

entries.name: @DEBUG
entries.purpose: start the DEBUG monitor

entries.name: HIGH$
entries.purpose: highest RAM address not in use

entries.name: OVRLY$
entries.purpose: system overlay now resident

entries.name: DAY$
entries.purpose: day of the year

entries.name: @DODIR
entries.purpose: display a directory, or put it in a buffer

entries.name: @FSPEC
entries.purpose: parse a file or device specification

entries.name: OSVER$
entries.purpose: version number of the operating system

entries.name: @INIT
entries.purpose: open a file or device, creating the file if it is new

entries.name: PDRV$
entries.purpose: physical address of the drive in use: 1, 2, 4, or 8
entries.note: the Model III text edition of the manual spells it PDRIV$

entries.name: @OPEN
entries.purpose: open an existing file

entries.name: LDRV$
entries.purpose: logical number, 0 to 7, of the drive in use
entries.note: the Model III text edition of the manual spells it LDRIV$

entries.name: @CLOSE
entries.purpose: close an open file

entries.name: SFLAG$
entries.purpose: system flag bits

entries.name: @KILL
entries.purpose: delete a file or device

entries.name: SVDAT1$
entries.purpose: year and day, packed
entries.note: the Model III map does not list it; the alphabetical listing (6-35) gives this address, and the purpose is the Model I map's for the same label (6-29)

entries.name: @LOAD
entries.purpose: load a program file into memory

entries.name: @RUN
entries.purpose: load a program file and start it

entries.name: @READ
entries.purpose: read a record from an open file

entries.name: @WRITE
entries.purpose: write a record to an open file

entries.name: @VER
entries.purpose: write a record, then read it back to verify it

entries.name: @REW
entries.purpose: rewind a file to its first record

entries.name: @POSN
entries.purpose: move a file to a chosen logical record

entries.name: @BKSP
entries.purpose: back up one logical record

entries.name: @PEOF
entries.purpose: position a file at its end

entries.name: @FEXT
entries.purpose: apply a default extension to a file specification

entries.name: @MULT
entries.purpose: multiply HL by A
entries.note: the Model III text edition of the manual spells it MULT

entries.name: @DIV
entries.purpose: divide HL by A
entries.note: the Model III text edition of the manual spells it DIVIDE

entries.name: @PARAM
entries.purpose: parse the optional parameters after a command

entries.name: SVDAT2$
entries.purpose: month, packed
entries.note: the Model III map does not list it; the alphabetical listing (6-35) gives this address, and the purpose is the Model I map's for the same label (6-29)

entries.name: @CKEOF
entries.purpose: check whether the file is at its end

entries.name: @WEOF
entries.purpose: write an end-of-file mark

entries.name: @RREAD
entries.purpose: read the current sector again

entries.name: @RWRIT
entries.purpose: write the current sector again

entries.name: @SKIP
entries.purpose: skip over the next record

entries.name: @DSPLY
entries.purpose: display a line of text on the screen

entries.name: @PRINT
entries.purpose: print a line of text on the printer

entries.name: @LOC
entries.purpose: work out the current logical record number

entries.name: @LOF
entries.purpose: work out the logical record number of the end of the file

entries.name: INTIM$
entries.purpose: copy of the interrupt latch

entries.name: INTMSK$
entries.purpose: interrupt mask storage next to INTIM$; the manual lists it by name and address only
entries.note: listed only in the alphabetical listing (6-35); neither memory map carries it

entries.name: INTVC$
entries.purpose: eight vectors, one for each bit of the interrupt latch
entries.note: the Model III text edition of the manual spells it INTVCT$; the map prints only the start address; the Model I map gives the area as 16 bytes (6-29)

entries.name: CFCB$
entries.purpose: file control block for commands

entries.name: TCB$
entries.purpose: interrupt task table

entries.name: DCT$
entries.purpose: area reserved for the drive code table

entries.name: SELECT
entries.purpose: select a different drive

entries.name: RSELCT
entries.purpose: test whether the requested drive is busy
entries.note: the Model III text edition of the manual spells it TSTBSY

entries.name: SEEK
entries.purpose: seek to a cylinder

entries.name: WRSECT
entries.purpose: write a sector
entries.note: the Model III text edition of the manual spells it WRSEC

entries.name: WRPROT
entries.purpose: write a system sector
entries.note: the Model III text edition of the manual spells it WRSYS

entries.name: WRTRK
entries.purpose: write a cylinder
entries.note: the Model III text edition of the manual spells it WRCYL

entries.name: VERSEC
entries.purpose: verify a sector

entries.name: RDSECT
entries.purpose: read a sector
entries.note: the Model III text edition of the manual spells it RDSEC

entries.name: GETDCT
entries.purpose: get the address of a drive code table entry

entries.name: DCTBYT
entries.purpose: get one field of a drive code table entry

entries.name: DIRRD
entries.purpose: read a directory record

entries.name: DIRWR
entries.purpose: write a directory record

entries.name: RDSSEC
entries.purpose: read a system sector

entries.name: DIRCYL
entries.purpose: get the directory cylinder number

entries.name: MULTEA
entries.purpose: multiply E by A

entries.name: DIVEA
entries.purpose: divide E by A

entries.name: USTOR$
entries.purpose: pointer to an 8-byte storage area for user programs
